open_points.subject: customer fiscal-data ownership
open_points.text: R0-37 says "fiscal data stays in PresuPro", while R0-80 says fiscal data joins Registry and "PresuPro keeps none".
open_points.question: Must later states treat Registry as the sole living store of tax id and legal name, with PresuPro retaining them only inside issued documents?
options: R0-80 fully overrides the R0-37 sentence
PresuPro may retain a separate fiscal-data record
Registry and PresuPro temporarily coexist until migration completes
open_points.default_guess: Treat R0-80 as the effective rule and remove PresuPro's living fiscal-data record.

open_points.subject: Client Portal offline projection
open_points.text: The Product statement says "no other service keeps a customer record or a copy of its values, except as fixed in a document it issued", but R0-39 lets Client Portal keep "the last projection it was permitted to keep locally" and `context` includes display name, address and `customer_ref`.
open_points.question: Which Registry values, if any, may Client Portal persist in its offline projection, and how is that exception reconciled with the one-home rule?
options: Permit a specifically enumerated offline-copy exception
Permit only non-personal fields in the offline projection
Remove persistent offline projection and fail while Registry is unavailable
open_points.default_guess: Permit only an explicitly enumerated Portal projection with no tax id or contact data, and state it as an exception to the one-home rule.

open_points.subject: customer erasure contents
open_points.text: "erase a customer's contact data" says only "name, phone, e-mail and language are gone", while R0-06 and R0-67 say the Customer keeps "only its identity and the fact that it was erased"; the record now also contains kind, tax id and legal name.
open_points.question: When a Customer is erased, are kind, tax id and legal name erased too, or do any of them survive?
options: Erase every field except `customer_ref` and the erased marker
Erase contact fields but retain kind and fiscal fields
Provide separate contact-data and fiscal-data erasures
open_points.default_guess: Erase every field except `customer_ref` and the erased marker.

open_points.subject: correction of customer kind and fiscal data
open_points.text: "correct a customer" promises only "the Customer with the new contact data", although Registry is the living owner of kind, tax id and legal name.
open_points.question: Which action changes a customer's kind, tax id or legal name after the Customer has been recorded?
options: Extend `correct a customer` to all mutable Customer fields
Add a separate fiscal-data correction action
Make kind and fiscal data immutable after creation
open_points.default_guess: Extend `correct a customer` to kind, contact data, tax id and legal name.

open_points.subject: object identifying characteristics
open_points.text: The trust-boundary section classifies "the object's address and identifying characteristics" as `personal_data`, but R0-80's sole-home rule names only "the object's address" and forbids other services from copying only "these values".
open_points.question: Are identifying characteristics subject to the same sole-living-copy and issued-document exception as the address?
options: Apply the sole-home rule to address and all identifying characteristics
Apply it only to the address
Declare which characteristics may be copied by each service
open_points.default_guess: Apply the sole-home rule to every object field classified as `personal_data`.

open_points.subject: personal data reaching the agent through other services
open_points.text: The Agent actor says it "never receives a value Registry holds as `personal_data`", but R0-74 says values that other cleared services pass to Kernel are "bounded by their own contracts, not here", and R0-76 gives Cabinet Registry data classified as `personal_data`.
open_points.question: Is "never reaches an agent" an end-to-end platform promise requiring explicit obligations on Cabinet, PresuPro and Client Portal, or only a promise about Registry's direct outputs to Kernel?
options: Make it an end-to-end promise and name the required downstream obligations
Narrow it to Registry-to-Kernel responses only
Remove personal-data access from services that can feed Kernel
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as an end-to-end promise and require Cabinet's contract to prohibit forwarding Registry personal data to Kernel or an agent.

open_points.subject: removal of existing service copies
open_points.text: R0-80 says "Removing the stores and copies the services keep today is each service's own change", while the Product statement already promises that no other service keeps such copies.
open_points.question: What observable condition must be met before Registry vNext may claim or enter operation under the one-home promise, and what happens if a dependent service still retains a living copy?
options: Block production cutover until every named service has removed its copies
Allow a declared migration period with temporary duplication
Treat removal as outside the release gate despite the product promise
open_points.default_guess: Gate production cutover on verified removal of the living copies from PresuPro, Client Portal and Cabinet.

open_points.subject: audit coverage
open_points.text: The audit promise uses "significant changes of state" and then names some categories, without saying whether publication and withdrawal, room creation, session registration, active-project changes, access requests and answers, imports, or failed mutations are entries.
open_points.question: Exactly which Primary actions and outcomes create audit entries?
options: Audit every accepted state-changing Primary action and every refused attempt
Audit every accepted state-changing Primary action only
Audit only the categories expressly enumerated in R0-58 and R0-66
open_points.default_guess: Audit every accepted state-changing Primary action, plus the explicitly required audit-erasure entry, and do not audit ordinary refusals unless separately classified as security events.

open_points.subject: revision checks for non-correction actions
open_points.text: R0-35 says "every accepted change" to a project or customer moves its revision and R0-29 says a change against an older revision is refused, but archive, customer erasure, restriction, relationship end/resume and project erasure do not state a revision input, next revision or stale-revision failure.
open_points.question: Do all of these actions require the current record revision and return the next revision, including actions described as idempotent when the target state already holds?
options: Require revisions for every project/customer mutation, with explicit no-op precedence
Require revisions only for correction forms
Use revisions for actual changes but allow idempotent repeats without checking them
open_points.default_guess: Require the current revision for every actual project/customer mutation, while explicit idempotent no-ops return unchanged even if the supplied revision is old.

open_points.subject: agent-session access concurrency
open_points.text: `read the session's access` returns "the access version", but grant, answer request, change active project and revoke do not say whether they take that version or how stale owner actions fail; R0-29 says every owner-interface change against an older revision is refused.
open_points.question: Is the access version an optimistic-concurrency precondition for every mutation of a session's grants, active project and pending request?
options: Require the current access version for every access mutation
Use it only as an informational change counter
Apply it to owner mutations but not Kernel request replacement or registration
open_points.default_guess: Require the current access version for owner mutations and define atomic version movement for Kernel registration and request replacement.

open_points.subject: projects included by the one-time import
open_points.text: R0-79 says "The owner picks the projects" and then names two projects "today"; after one successful import the operation is permanently closed.
open_points.question: Is the successful import required to contain exactly those two named projects, may it contain either subset, or may the owner select any VPS projects present at migration time?
options: Exactly the two named project ids
Any subset of the two named project ids
Any owner-selected VPS projects
open_points.default_guess: Require exactly the two named project ids in the single successful import.

open_points.subject: anonymised project artifact pointers
open_points.text: R0-62 says an anonymised project keeps all artifact pointers, R0-68 says a pointer value that improperly contains personal data "is not refused and does reach the agent", while R0-71 says an anonymised project "holds no personal value".
open_points.question: Before anonymisation, must Registry remove or reject pointers containing identifying values, must the owner attest that they are clean, or is the no-personal-value claim limited to fields Registry classifies as `personal_data`?
options: Validate or remove identifying pointer values before anonymisation
Require an owner attestation and keep pointers unchanged
Limit the guarantee to formally classified fields even if pointer text identifies someone
open_points.default_guess: Require the owner to confirm that retained pointers permit no re-identification and refuse anonymisation otherwise.

open_points.subject: legacy VPS migration source
open_points.text: The Actors section defines every non-production instance as a test instance that holds "no production personal data", while R0-79 names the existing Registry on the VPS as the migration source for projects, customers and objects containing production personal data.
open_points.question: What actor and trust boundary describes the legacy VPS Registry during export and migration, before it is retired?
options: A separately named trusted legacy-production source
A test instance exceptionally allowed to hold production data during migration
Part of the new production trust boundary until cutover
open_points.default_guess: Name it as a temporary trusted legacy-production source with production personal data, distinct from test instances.

open_points.subject: migration export and uploaded file lifecycle
open_points.text: R0-72 says Registry defines and accepts an uploaded migration file containing customers, objects and links, but says only that "the source keeps none after the migration"; it does not say whether production retains the upload after success or failure.
open_points.question: Is the migration file stored by Registry, and when is every temporary or failed-upload copy destroyed?
options: Process it transiently and destroy it after every attempt
Retain it until the single import succeeds
Retain an archival copy as migration evidence
open_points.default_guess: Process the upload transiently and delete it after either success or failure, retaining only the resulting records and non-personal audit entry.
